QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_8

question.text: A PE secondary intermediary pitches Brahmaputra Growth Partners on a transaction where the GP rolls TWO mature portfolio companies out of the existing fund into a new vehicle backed by a secondary buyer — LPs choose to cash out or roll. This structure is BEST described as:

answer.text: A recapitalisation of the fund via dividend recap
A strip sale of minority interests

explanation.text: The Logic: In private equity secondaries terminology, a GP-led multi-asset continuation vehicle is a structure in which the existing fund's general partner moves more than one portfolio company out of the legacy fund into a newly formed vehicle that the same GP continues to manage, with a secondary buyer providing fresh capital and existing LPs given the option to either take cash for their interests or roll their position into the new vehicle. Where multiple assets are rolled, the structure is referred to as a multi-asset continuation vehicle; a single rolled asset is referred to as a single-asset continuation vehicle. The Trap: An LP-led secondary is an investor-side sale of fund interests and does not involve restructuring of the portfolio at the fund level. A dividend recapitalisation increases debt at a single portfolio company to fund a distribution and is not a fund-level secondary transaction. A strip sale of minority interests moves only a pro-rata slice of selected assets at the fund level and is distinct from a full continuation-vehicle structure. Note: The cited workbook chapter discusses portfolio-company exit routes such as IPO, secondary or trade sale, strategic sale, buyback, liquidation and investor-interest secondaries, but does not explicitly cover GP-led multi-asset continuation vehicles, cash-or-roll mechanics, fairness opinions or LPAC waivers. The framing above reflects general private-equity secondaries practice rather than a direct workbook citation.
